newsitem.title: UK: UK's Clarke rejects giveaway budget.
newsitem.headline: UK's Clarke rejects giveaway budget.

text.p: Britain's Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said in an interview published on Friday he would not introduce any measures in his November budget that might have to be reversed after the election.
"I propose to do nothing in this budget that might run the risk of having to be reversed after the election," he told London's Evening Standard newspaper.
Clarke will deliver his budget on November 26. The Conservative government must call an election by May 1997.
"Tax cuts can only happen if they are in the interests of the economy," Clarke said.
With the Conservative Party lagging opposition Labour badly in opinion polls, Clarke is under pressure to cut taxes and interest rates to boost his party's fortunes.

Clarke denied he felt isolated within the party after a row this week over his attitude to European Economic and Monetary Union. On Monday, Clarke said it would be "pathetic" for Britain to skulk on the sidelines while EMU went ahead in 1999.
"There are stacks of Conservative members who agree with me," Clarke told the Evening Standard.
He was interviewed in Bermuda where he was attending a conference of Commonwealth finance ministers.
